title: ZeroSOC Case
description: A ZeroSOC Case: the subset of the OCSF Incident Finding [2005] fields the framework uses, plus the framework's own fields under 'zerosoc', the ZeroSOC extension to OCSF (declared in ocsf_extension/). The Case is identified by metadata.correlation_uid. A Case becomes an Incident when verdict_id = 2. See case_schema.md. A property this schema does not name is an attribute of the OCSF class, used as OCSF defines it; a source's own record is under 'unmapped', keyed by the source.

additionalProperties.description: An attribute of the OCSF class the framework does not state, used as OCSF defines it.

message.description: The Case title: the source's own title for the Case, which it may change as alerts join; the first Alert's title where the source gives none.

assignee.description: The Case assignee: the executor responsible for advancing the Case and for its verdict.

desc.description: The Case Summary: what happened and when, the entities involved and which acted on which, and the root cause once established.

notes.description: Notes on the Case, among them the Triage Note and the Investigation Note: renderings of the Case at their gate.

finding_info_list.description: Every entry of the Case's record: the Alerts first, then the result of every check and validation query, and the response actions taken on the Case.

attacks.description: The Incident's tactics and techniques, assessed at incident confirmation from the Observations that stand and kept current as the response reveals more. Empty until confirmation: the techniques the Alerts assert are provisional and stay on the Alerts.

observables.description: Normalized entities — the join keys of the investigation.

start_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). The earliest event or observation that contributed to the Case. It opens at the earliest Alert's own start_time and moves earlier whenever a Malicious Observation cites an earlier event; a benign precursor examined and ruled out contributed to the investigation and not to the Case, and never moves it. On a confirmed Incident this is T0, the earliest confirmed malicious event. On a Case closed as a False Positive or a Benign Positive it is still the earliest Alert's own start and nothing more: nothing malicious was confirmed, so it is not T0 and anchors no metric.

end_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). The most recent event or observation that contributed to the Case.

vendor_attributes.description: The Case's severity as the source reports it, or the highest of its alerts' where the source reports none, kept current while the Case is open; never a value the executor wrote back.

tickets.description: Tickets the Case raised; a False Positive raises one of kind tuning to Phase 1, a Benign close one of kind exception, the Knowledge Base entry a person confirms.

unmapped.description: OCSF's container for source-specific attributes: one object per source, keyed by the source's own identifier, its shape declared by that source's own description and validated against it. Anything OCSF or the framework carries is a mapping, and never here.

uid.description: Where the event is in OCSF, its metadata.uid.

type.description: Used instead of type_uid where the event is not in OCSF.

count.description: How many occurrences this one reference stands for.

created_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

first_seen_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). When the event happened. The Case's start_time is the earliest of these across its Malicious Observations.

last_seen_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

process.description: The process the event shows, where it shows one.

script.description: The decoded command the event's process ran, where it ran an encoded one.

ocsf_related_event.description: An event that is evidence of the Observation: what the Observation rests on, kept with the Case and cited by identifier. It may be any OCSF event — a Detection Finding where the Observation is an Alert, a Remediation Activity on an action entry, an event of the telemetry a query returned — or an event that is not in OCSF at all, which `type` names instead of `type_uid`. What is left out is what the Observation did not rest on: bulk telemetry, result sets, message bodies, file content.

created_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

first_seen_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). When the thing the Observation reports was first observed, which is not when the Observation was made. The Case Timeline orders on this, and the Case's start_time is the earliest of them.

last_seen_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). When it was last observed.

attacks.description: The tactics and techniques the entry shows. An Alert carries the ones its detection asserted, and a Malicious Observation SHOULD carry the ones it shows.

types.description: What the entry rests on: alert for an aggregated Alert, event for the result of a check or query, action for a response action.

traits.description: Characteristics of the entity the Observation is about, surfaced from the event. On an Alert this is where the threat name and family the detection assigned are carried: category 'malware', name the family, values the threat names the source assigned.

zerosoc.description: Framework attributes of an Observation: its side and confidence, whether the Case Timeline renders it, and an Alert's alert type. An Observation that bears on no hypothesis carries neither side nor confidence, and so does every action entry.

side.description: The hypothesis the Observation bears on. Absent where it is pure context.

confidence_id.description: Weighs 1, 2 and 3 in hypothesis resolution. Present exactly when side is.

timeline.description: Set on the entries the Case Timeline renders.

alert_type.description: On an Alert, the alert type it is triaged under: the one its source declares, or the one the executor identified. Absent where no alert type describes the Alert, and on every entry that is not an Alert.

ocsf_finding_info.description: One entry of the Case's record: an Observation — an Alert, or the result of a check or validation query — or a response action taken on the Case.

title.description: What the ticket asks for, in a line. Rendered by the Note's Response Actions element.

type_id.description: Which system holds the ticket, not what it is for.

type.description: The type_id caption, as OCSF names it: Internal or External.

status_id.description: Where the ticket stands. A planned remediation is open; one the Case acted on is resolved.

zerosoc.description: Framework attributes of a ticket the Case raised.

kind.description: What the ticket is for, which OCSF's type_id does not say. The framework names tuning, visibility, containment, eradication and recovery; the set is open while the response phase is still being designed.

ocsf_ticket.description: A ticket the Case raised. Borrowed from OCSF and intentionally open, so a platform's full ticket object validates unchanged.

ocsf_trait.description: The list of key traits or characteristics extracted from the observation, as the source stated them. What a trait holds depends on the observation it came from; the framework reserves no category and no name.

name.description: The trait's name, as the source stated it.

category.description: The grouping the trait belongs to, where the source gives one.

values.description: The threat names the source assigned.

reclassification_pivots.description: Every change of candidate Incident Category, with the evidence that triggered it.

deadline.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

anyOf.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

watch_until.description: OCSF timestamp_t: monitoring watch on the Case's entities after an Insufficient Data or Low-confidence close.

master_case_uid.description: Set on a Duplicate close: the open master Case that handles the activity, by its metadata.correlation_uid.

ocsf_analytic.description: What produced the Observation: the detection content that raised an Alert, the check that answered a triage question, or the validation query that tested a hypothesis. An Observation and what produced it are never separated.

uid.description: The identifier of the check or query, where it has one; the event reference the Note cites for it otherwise.

name.description: The question it answers, in the words a reader of the Case understands — never the query language.

type.description: What kind of analytic it is, where `type_id` is Other: `triage check`, `validation query`, `enrichment`.

type_id.description: OCSF's analytic type, which OCSF requires. A triage check and a validation query are none of OCSF's listed types, so they are Other (99) and `type` names them.

desc.description: What was asked, as the executor asked it — the telemetry, the entities and the window — before any tool translated it.

algorithm.description: The query the tool actually ran, in that tool's own language. It is what makes the Observation reproducible by someone holding neither the Case nor the executor.

uid.description: The entity's value as it appears in observables.

target.description: The node uid of the entity acted on.

relation.description: Where the edge is an observed technique, the most specific identifier the Observation's attacks carries for it, whose entry gives the edge its tactic; otherwise a STIX 2.1 relationship type.

title.description: The deliverable's name, per the naming convention.

comment.description: The rendering of the Case at this gate.

created_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

modified_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

ocsf_process.description: A process an Observation rests on, with its parentage in parent_process and ancestry. A parent the evidence does not show carries what is known of it.

cmd_line.description: The command line as the process was launched, encoded or not.

created_time.description: OCSF timestamp_t: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

ancestry.description: The extended parentage, the direct parent first.

ocsf_script.description: A command decoded from its encoded form.

script_content.description: The decoded content, normalized to UTF-8.

hashes.description: Hashes of the script in its original encoding.

parent_uid.description: The uid of the script that launched this one.

ocsf_metadata.description: OCSF's metadata of the Case. The framework states its correlation_uid: the Case's identifier, the same on every event of the Case.

correlation_uid.description: Case identifier, cited by the Notes, tuning tickets and metrics.
